summary: Build practical LXD and instructional design skills with ADDIE, SAM, storyboards, and evaluation tools. Enrol today.
lede: Learning experience design and instructional design helps you turn performance needs into aligned learning journeys, practical activities, and evidence of competence. This course develops your ability to use ADDIE, Bloom’s Taxonomy, action mapping, learner analysis, measurable objectives, assessment alignment, and evaluation planning. You will work through a structured design process to create needs analyses, design blueprints, storyboards, facilitator guides, assessments, and usable learning products. The course also addresses realistic constraints such as limited budgets, tight deadlines, existing content, legacy LMS structures, stakeholder input, accessibility planning, and AI-supported rapid drafting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape learning solutions, manage training quality, and translate business needs into practical instructional outputs.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of workplace training, adult learning concepts, or learning and development processes. Experience with course creation, facilitation, or learning coordination is helpful, but no programming or coding is required. If you already design modules, manage LMS content, or brief subject matter experts, you will be able to apply the exercises immediately. Familiarity with Microsoft PowerPoint, Microsoft Word, or a learning authoring environment such as Articulate 360 will support the hands-on work. Advanced concepts such as accessibility design, evaluation strategy, and AI-supported drafting are taught at operational application level, not technical engineering level.
